post.title: About 80% of Keurig's U.S. Coffee Sales Are Pods
post.ig:
Keurig's real business is the pod, not the machine.
Keurig Dr Pepper's U.S. Coffee segment sold $3.99 billion in 2025; K-Cup pods were $3.21 billion of it (about 80%, our math).
Segment adjusted (non-GAAP) operating margin: 30.9% in 2025.
In 2014, Keurig 2.0 brewers rejected unlicensed pods; in Keurig's fiscal Q2 2015 (ended March 2015), brewer and accessory sales fell 23% from a year earlier.
Our math: an example pod price of $1.97/oz is $31.52/lb, vs. a $9.46/lb BLS average for ground coffee in February 2026.
In 2026, Keurig Dr Pepper closed its JDE Peet's acquisition, part of a plan to split coffee into its own company.
Sources: Keurig Dr Pepper 2025 Form 10-K and Q4 2025 release; Keurig Green Mountain Q2 FY2015 results; BLS average prices; KDP release, Apr 1, 2026.
